dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/12/Text/2] The final goal of Study 1 was to examine the correlations between depression and both academic performance and school conduct. Specifically, we expected that more depressed children would have poorer academic achievement and more conduct problems. [/page/12/Text/3] There was a significant correlation between the CDI and poor academic achievement in Chinese children, r = 0.25, p < .001. More depressed children had poorer academic achievement.

Source.evidence_source: [/page/12/Text/3] There was a significant correlation between the CDI and poor academic achievement in Chinese children, r = 0.25, p < .001. More depressed children had poorer academic achievement. The results also showed that children's CDI scores were significantly correlated with worse social conduct as measured by the CCQ: r = 0.44, p < .001.
